column1:
sysctl net.ipv4.ip_forward
Check whether IPv4 routing is enabled.
column2:
Reads the current net.ipv4.ip_forward value. 1 enables forwarding between interfaces; 0 disables it. This command only reads the setting.
sysctl: Read or change running kernel settings.
IPv4: Internet Protocol version 4, a network addressing system.
Forwarding: Passing traffic from one network interface to another.
Kernel: The operating system’s core.

column1:
ip neigh show
Show nearby network address mappings.
column2:
Displays the IPv4 and IPv6 neighbour table, including interface names and entry states. Entries may be incomplete or stale; this is not a complete list of reachable hosts.
Neighbour table: Cached mappings between nearby network addresses and link-layer addresses.
IPv4/IPv6: Versions 4 and 6 of Internet Protocol.
Interface: A physical or virtual network connection.
Link-layer address: A local network identifier, such as an Ethernet MAC address.

column1:
sudo firewall-cmd --permanent --list-all
Show saved firewall settings for the default zone.
column2:
--permanent reads saved firewalld configuration rather than the current runtime configuration. Without --zone, --list-all shows the default zone’s settings, not every zone.
firewalld: Software managing Linux firewall rules.
Zone: A named firewall policy assigned to connections or sources.
Runtime: Settings currently in use.
sudo: Run an authorized command as another user, usually the administrator.

column1:
sudo firewall-cmd --get-active-zones
Show which firewall zones are in use.
column2:
Lists active firewalld zones and their associated interfaces or source addresses. This is a runtime view.
firewalld: Software managing Linux firewall rules.
Zone: A named firewall policy.
Interface: A physical or virtual network connection.
Runtime: Settings currently in use.
sudo: Run an authorized command as another user.

column1:
sudo nmcli connection modify ens18 connection.zone drop
Assign the ens18 connection to the drop zone.
column2:
Changes the saved NetworkManager profile named ens18 to use firewalld’s drop zone. Zone changes can take effect immediately for an active profile. The standard drop zone silently discards unsolicited incoming traffic; this can affect remote access.
nmcli: NetworkManager’s command-line tool.
NetworkManager: Software managing network connections.
Profile: A saved collection of connection settings.
firewalld: Software managing firewall rules.
Zone: A named firewall policy.
sudo: Run an authorized command as another user.

column1:
sudo nmcli connection up ens18
Activate the ens18 connection profile.
column2:
Activates the NetworkManager profile named ens18, applying its connection settings. The profile name may differ from the device name. Reactivation can interrupt traffic or remote access.
nmcli: NetworkManager’s command-line tool.
Profile: Saved network connection settings.
Activation: Bringing a connection into use.
sudo: Run an authorized command as another user.

column1:
getent ahostsv4 redhat.com
Look up IPv4 addresses for redhat.com.
column2:
Queries configured system name services for IPv4 addresses associated with redhat.com. The output can repeat an address for different socket types; a successful lookup does not prove the site is reachable.
getent: Retrieve entries using system-configured lookup services.
IPv4: Internet Protocol version 4.
Name service: A source used to translate names into addresses, such as DNS.
DNS: Domain Name System.
Socket type: The kind of communication endpoint, such as a stream or datagram.

column1:
sudo qm help set | grep -A 12 -- '--net[n]'
Search virtual-machine network-option help.
column2:
Reads qm set help and shows each grep match plus 12 following lines. As written, the regular expression --net[n] matches --netn, not the literal --net[n]. To find the literal help label, use grep -F -A 12 -- '--net[n]'. The -- ends grep option parsing.
qm: Proxmox’s virtual-machine management tool.
grep: A text-search program.
Regular expression: A pattern describing matching text.
Pipe (
): Pass one command’s output into another.
sudo: Run an authorized command as another user.

column1:
sudo qm help set | grep -A 15 'trunks='
Find VLAN trunk settings in Proxmox help.
column2:
Reads qm set help, finds trunks= and includes 15 following lines. This inspects help without changing a virtual machine.
qm: Proxmox’s virtual-machine management tool.
grep: A text-search program.
Pipe (
): Pass one command’s output into another.
VLAN: Virtual Local Area Network, a logical network separation.
Trunk: A link carrying traffic for multiple VLANs.
sudo: Run an authorized command as another user.

column1:
sudo qm set 101 --net1 'virtio=BC:24:11:D9:A0:51,bridge=vmbr1,firewall=1,trunks=100;200;300;400'
Configure VM 101’s second network adapter.
column2:
Sets or replaces net1 on VM 101: VirtIO model, the specified MAC address, bridge vmbr1, Proxmox firewall flag enabled, and VLAN trunks 100, 200, 300 and 400. Quotes keep the semicolons inside one argument. Check existing adapter options first; this does not create guest VLAN interfaces or guarantee effective firewall filtering.
VM: Virtual machine, a software-defined computer.
VirtIO: Efficient virtual hardware designed for virtual machines.
MAC: Media Access Control address, a network adapter’s link-layer identifier.
Bridge: A software network switch.
VLAN: Virtual Local Area Network.
Trunk: A connection carrying multiple VLANs.
sudo: Run an authorized command as another user.

column1:
sudo qm status 101
Check whether VM 101 is running.
column2:
Shows the current state of Proxmox virtual machine 101, such as running or stopped. A running state does not prove its operating system or network is healthy.
qm: Proxmox’s virtual-machine management tool.
VM: Virtual machine, a software-defined computer.
sudo: Run an authorized command as another user.

column1:
sudo qm config 101 --current | grep '^net'
Show VM 101’s current network configuration.
column2:
--current requests the current configuration rather than including pending changes. grep selects lines beginning with net, showing configured network-adapter entries. This does not inspect settings inside the guest.
qm: Proxmox’s virtual-machine management tool.
VM: Virtual machine.
Pending change: A saved change not yet applied.
Guest: The operating system running inside a virtual machine.
Pipe (
): Pass output to another command.
^: Match the start of a line.
sudo: Run an authorized command as another user.

column1:
sudo nmcli connection add type vlan \
con-name vlan100-management \
ifname ens19.100 \
dev ens19 \
id 100 \
ipv4.method manual \
ipv4.addresses 10.20.10.1/24 \
ipv4.never-default yes \
ipv6.method disabled \
connection.zone drop \
connection.autoconnect no
Create a saved management VLAN connection.
column2:
Adds profile vlan100-management on parent ens19, with interface ens19.100 and VLAN ID 100. Assigns static IPv4 address 10.20.10.1/24, prevents an IPv4 default route, disables IPv6, selects the drop firewall zone and disables automatic connection. It creates a profile; activate it separately when ready. The outer double quotes in the source are treated as document formatting, not part of the executable command.
nmcli: NetworkManager’s command-line tool.
Profile: Saved connection settings.
VLAN: Virtual Local Area Network, a logical separation of network traffic.
Parent interface: The underlying network connection carrying a VLAN.
IPv4/IPv6: Internet Protocol versions 4 and 6.
/24: A network prefix using the first 24 address bits.
Default route: The route used when no more specific route matches.
Zone: A named firewall policy.
Autoconnect: Starting a saved connection automatically.
Backslash (\): Continue a shell command on the next line.
sudo: Run an authorized command as another user.

column1:
ip -d link show ens19.100
Inspect details of the VLAN interface.
column2:
Shows detailed link information for ens19.100. -d includes extra details such as the VLAN ID and parent relationship when available. This checks the live interface, not just its saved profile.
Interface: A physical or virtual network connection.
VLAN: Virtual Local Area Network.
Link: The network connection represented by an interface.
Profile: Saved network connection settings.

column1:
sudo nmcli device reapply ens18
Apply supported profile changes to ens18.
column2:
Asks NetworkManager to reapply supported changes from the active connection’s saved profile to device ens18 without first taking it down. Some changes cannot be reapplied and need reactivation.
nmcli: NetworkManager’s command-line tool.
Profile: Saved network connection settings.
Reactivation: Starting a connection again to apply its settings.
sudo: Run an authorized command as another user.

column1:
nmcli -f .... connection show <profile>
Show selected settings from a connection profile.
column2:
Incomplete template: replace .... with comma-separated field names and <profile> with a real profile name or identifier. -f chooses output fields. For example: nmcli -f connection.id,connection.autoconnect connection show ens18. Do not type the angle brackets; the shell treats them as redirection operators.
nmcli: NetworkManager’s command-line tool.
Field: One named item in command output.
Profile: Saved network connection settings.
Shell: The program that interprets typed commands.
Redirection: Sending command input or output to another location.

column1:
nmcli -f NAME,TYPE,DEVICE,AUTOCONNECT connection show
List profiles with their automatic-start settings.
column2:
Selects NAME, TYPE, DEVICE and AUTOCONNECT columns when listing NetworkManager profiles. Includes inactive profiles; a profile name need not match its device name.
nmcli: NetworkManager’s command-line tool.
Profile: Saved network connection settings.
Device: A network interface.
Autoconnect: Automatically starting a suitable saved connection.

column1:
sudo bridge vlan show dev fwpr101p1
Inspect VLAN settings on one bridge port.
column2:
Shows Linux bridge VLAN entries for fwpr101p1, rather than every port. Check membership, the PVID and whether traffic leaves untagged. The named device must exist.
Bridge: A software network switch.
Port: An interface attached to a bridge.
VLAN: Virtual Local Area Network.
PVID: Port VLAN Identifier, used for incoming untagged traffic.
Untagged: Carrying no VLAN label.
sudo: Run an authorized command as another user.

column1:
ip -6 addr show dev ens18
Show IPv6 addresses on ens18.
column2:
-6 restricts the display to IPv6; addr show dev ens18 restricts it to that device. Displays currently assigned addresses and their details.
IPv6: Internet Protocol version 6, using 128-bit network addresses.
Device: A network interface.
Interface: A physical or virtual network connection.

column1:
sudo ss -lntp
Show listening TCP ports and their programs.
column2:
-l selects listening sockets, -n keeps addresses and ports numeric, -t selects TCP and -p shows process information when permitted. This does not show UDP listeners or prove a port is reachable through a firewall.
ss: A tool for inspecting network sockets.
Socket: A communication endpoint used by a program.
TCP: Transmission Control Protocol, a reliable network transport.
UDP: User Datagram Protocol, a datagram-based network transport.
Process: A running program.
sudo: Run an authorized command as another user.

column1:
sudo nmcli connection modify ens18 ipv6.method disabled
Disable IPv6 in the ens18 connection profile.
column2:
Changes the saved profile named ens18 so NetworkManager disables IPv6 for that connection. Apply the change through supported reapplication or reactivation; this does not globally disable IPv6 on the host.
nmcli: NetworkManager’s command-line tool.
Profile: Saved network connection settings.
IPv6: Internet Protocol version 6.
Host: The computer running these settings.
sudo: Run an authorized command as another user.

column1:
sudo nmcli connection modify vlan400-peripherals connection.autoconnect yes
Allow the peripherals connection to start automatically.
column2:
Sets connection.autoconnect to yes for profile vlan400-peripherals. Allows NetworkManager to activate it automatically when suitable; does not itself guarantee immediate activation.
nmcli: NetworkManager’s command-line tool.
Profile: Saved network connection settings.
Autoconnect: Automatically starting a saved connection.
sudo: Run an authorized command as another user.

column1:
sudo qm listsnapshot 101
List snapshots for VM 101.
column2:
Corrected source typo: the sheet says sudo qm listsnaphot 101; the valid subcommand is listsnapshot. Lists snapshots for Proxmox virtual machine 101.
qm: Proxmox’s virtual-machine management tool.
VM: Virtual machine, a software-defined computer.
Snapshot: A saved point-in-time state used for recovery or comparison; it is not an independent backup.
sudo: Run an authorized command as another user.

column1:
sudo qm rollback 101 <snapshot-name>
Restore VM 101 to a named snapshot.
column2:
Rolls back virtual machine 101 to the selected snapshot, discarding later changes to the state covered by that snapshot. Replace <snapshot-name> with a real name without angle brackets. Check the target and preserve needed current data before running.
qm: Proxmox’s virtual-machine management tool.
VM: Virtual machine.
Snapshot: A saved point-in-time state.
Rollback: Return to an earlier saved state.
sudo: Run an authorized command as another user.

column1:
sudo journalctl -u NetworkManager -b --no-pager
Read NetworkManager logs from this boot.
column2:
-u selects the NetworkManager service, -b selects the current boot and --no-pager prints directly instead of opening an interactive viewer. Useful when investigating activation or configuration errors.
journalctl: A tool for reading the systemd event journal.
systemd: Linux’s system and service manager.
Journal: A system record of events and messages.
Boot: A startup of the operating system.
Pager: An interactive text viewer.
sudo: Run an authorized command as another user.

column1:
sudo sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_forward=0
Turn off IPv4 routing now.
column2:
-w writes 0 to net.ipv4.ip_forward, disabling IPv4 forwarding between interfaces in the running kernel. This can stop traffic routed through a firewall or gateway. It does not save a persistent setting across reboots and does not control IPv6 forwarding.
sysctl: Read or change kernel settings.
IPv4/IPv6: Internet Protocol versions 4 and 6.
Forwarding: Passing traffic between interfaces.
Kernel: The operating system’s core.
Gateway: A system routing traffic between networks.
sudo: Run an authorized command as another user.
